title: A track fed by another is not released when the feeding track's input device disconnects
body:
Found while reviewing #304.

`TrackManager.onMidiEvent` matches only `DeviceTrackInputSpec` / `DeviceTrackOutputSpec`, so it
reaches the tracks wired straight to a device and no further along inter-track links.

For a chain `A(input = device Y, output = ToTrack(B))` → `B(output = device Z)`, unplugging Y calls
`A.releaseInput()` only:

- the per-channel release A sends (Hold off, Sostenuto off, All Notes Off) is forwarded into **B's
  pipeline input**, where `MpeTuner.process` routes it through `MpeMessageRouting.roleOf` / `route`
  and discards whatever falls outside B's input zone;
- B's own `Tuner` and `TuningChanger`s are never reset, so B's note state stays stale and device Z
  can keep notes held.

The same asymmetry applies to `MidiDeviceOpenedEvent`: when Z opens, only B is reset, not A.

## Possible fix

Propagate the release and the reset transitively along `ToTrackOutputSpec` / `FromTrackInputSpec`
links, rather than only to the tracks that name a device.

## Notes

Pre-existing gap in the hot-plug work of #131, which deliberately scoped itself to the tracks wired
directly to a device. Related: #296, #297 and #298 record the other known inter-track wiring gaps,
and #303 covers restoring the tuning after a reset.
